answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 26% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the attacker's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the delta reward in the nadir ledger costs the operator directly, and the fable audit records each payout. A farm of 268 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
